title: Empty Trace Export Check (Traces Without Spans Are Dropped)
dataSources: Captured trace objects from `SplunkAOLogger(ingestion_hook=captured.append)` in the agent's unit tests; no tenant or project is needed
description: Catches code paths that start a trace but never add a span. Splunk Agent Observability exports spans only, so a trace with no spans is silently dropped and the request disappears from the stream.
value: Prevents silent gaps in the agent record. Without this test, an error path or an early return can drop whole requests while `export_health` still reports healthy, and nobody notices until an incident review finds no trace.
implementation: In the agent's test suite, build the logger with `ingestion_hook=captured.append`, run each request path (including error paths), and assert that `captured[0].traces[0]` has at least one span. Fail the build when a path produces a trace with no spans.
visualization: Unit test results in the CI pipeline for each request path.
knownFalsePositives: A request path that intentionally does no agent work (for example a health probe) has no spans by design. Exclude it from the test rather than adding an empty span.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

Export is OpenTelemetry and carries spans only; the trace is their container. A trace with no child spans is never exported, there is no error, and `export_health` stays healthy. Pass `ingestion_hook=captured.append` to `SplunkAOLogger` in tests so nothing is uploaded and no project is needed.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

Nothing to configure in the console. The check runs in the agent's own test suite, before the code reaches the Agent Stream.

Step 3 — Validate

Run the test against the normal path and against each error path. `captured[0].traces[0]` holds the trace with `status_code`, `output` and `spans`. Using the hook for error paths also keeps junk traces out of the real stream. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Run the test in CI on every change to the request handler, and add a case for each new route or tool loop.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

Test passes but traces are still missing in the console: check that spans are concluded (open spans are not exported) and allow 30 to 60 seconds of indexing lag. Empty spans list: add an agent span at the call site before any early return.
grandmaExplanation: We test that every question the assistant answers leaves a written record behind, because a record with no steps in it gets thrown away without warning.

productArtifacts.title: Offline test: every request path exports at least one span
productArtifacts.body:
from splunk_ao import SplunkAOLogger

def test_request_path_exports_spans():
    captured = []
    logger = SplunkAOLogger(ingestion_hook=captured.append)  # nothing is uploaded
    handle_request(logger, "What is the status of order 42?")
    trace = captured[0].traces[0]
    assert trace.spans, "trace has no spans and would never be exported"
